text:
Clayton Keller has 22 points in 17 games, 18 of them assists and 16 on the power play. That last number tells you where Utah's captain is doing his damage. At five on five the picture is stranger: the Mammoth take 55.3% of shot attempts with him on but just 49% of the expected goals, 11.8 points worse than without him. Plenty of pucks, not many good ones.

He hasn't scored since Oct. 19, but he has seven assists in a four-game point streak, three of them in the win over Toronto on Nov. 3. His shooting (9.8%) sits below the middle of his range (12.3%), so a goal or two should come.

Last season says the even-strength issue should sort itself out. Evolving-Hockey had him sixth among 401 forwards at 3.5 wins above replacement, driving play at the 88th percentile, with the caveat that his results ran ahead of his chances. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 11.4 primary shot assists per 60, 98th percentile. Watch his five-on-five share over the next month; the power play can't do it all.
headline: Keller's power play is carrying the line
